title: Relic Tide
tagline: Real-time 2–4 player extraction game in Godot: 20 Hz authoritative server, filtered snapshots, seeded rounds, receipted art pipeline.
summary: Relic Tide is a real-time online extraction game for 2–4 players in a flooding ruin, built in Godot 4 and GDScript with a headless authoritative room service. The repo documents 20 Hz rules, recipient-filtered snapshots at 10 Hz, direction-only movement packets, bounded client prediction and seeded rounds, plus receipts for paid PixelLab requests and recorded prompts and hashes for generated images and local depth maps. Verification is local: Godot suites, socket tests and browser captures. There is no WAN playtest or public deployment.

aiRole.summary: AI tooling appears in three forms in this repository. Agent guidance files and hooks are checked in: AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and a .claude/ folder with Graft hooks, all telling agents to query a code graph before reading source. The first design prompt is stored in prompt-used/#001.md, and the asset pipeline records generators: PixelLab for sprites and animation, the built-in image generator for backgrounds, props and doors, local Depth-Anything-V2 for depth maps, and a paid DepthFlow service that was tried and rejected. The repo also records its verification: headless Godot suites with counts, real-socket network scenarios, native and browser captures and an independent visual reviewer's disposition. Those results are the repo's reports; this review re-ran none of them.

narrative.problem:
Relic Tide began, in the prompt stored at prompt-used/#001.md, as a board-game-inspired exploration game for two to four players in which a ruined city rises from and sinks into water, and players choose actions without knowing what the others will do. The repository's later documents replace simultaneous turns with real-time play: explorers move continuously through a flooding ruin, take relics and return to a boat, and only extracted treasure scores. There is no assigned traitor role.

The engineering problem the documents describe is social play over a network. Helping, blocking and abandoning others must happen through visible world actions. The server must own doors, water, relic ownership and outcomes, and clients must not receive what they could use to cheat: hidden positions, rivals' inventories or puzzle answers.
narrative.approach:
The documents fix a split of responsibilities. A central room service owns movement validation, world objects, flood state, relic ownership and extraction, and clients send intentions, not positions, water levels or scores. Domain rules live in a class with no scene, timer, input or rendering dependency, so tests can drive it with supplied ticks.

The game is written in Godot 4 with GDScript and exported to the browser (single-threaded Compatibility renderer, WebGL 2). Art is raster: environment sheets, props and sprites from generators, animated in code, with recorded prompts, hashes and receipts. The project rules forbid drawing scenery or explorers from polygons or procedural shapes.
narrative.architecture:
At runtime there are three parts. The client runs main.gd for presentation, movement_client.gd for local prediction and session.gd for the WebSocket link. A headless Godot process (server/room_server.gd) runs the same session script in server mode and hosts room_directory.gd, which owns room codes, membership, validation and one rules object per match. A small Node script (web/serve.mjs) serves the exported game and forwards WebSocket upgrades on /rooms to that loopback server and starts it.

Geometry is shared: expedition_map.gd defines each level once, and both client prediction and server rules instantiate it for the match. player_view.gd turns authoritative state into a per-recipient snapshot. The room service is GDScript running in Godot, not a separate Node application.
narrative.implementation:
Each 0.05 s step runs in a fixed order: vault holds, doors, valve holds, water, movement against current collision and water, survival and extraction, then hunters. Doors advance before water, so a refuge door that finishes closing in a tick admits no water in that tick. Water moves by simultaneous transfers from the previous state. Movement packets carry a direction, a sequence number and a match token, and the server rejects any other shape.

Snapshots are built per recipient and sent on every second tick and after accepted events. Unseen explorers are sent as a name and a hidden state. The client predicts at most 12 unacknowledged steps, then resets to the acknowledged position and replays the rest. Rounds are seeded from four random bytes taken by the room service, which fix duration, breach and hunt timing and chest rewards. Hunters get one target each and give up after 2.5 seconds without sight or beyond 900 units.

The asset pipeline in tools/assets wraps PixelLab, local Depth-Anything-V2 and Aseprite. It writes a receipt before any paid request, refuses to overwrite a versioned bundle and records source hashes in manifests.
narrative.outcome:
At the pinned commit the repository holds three authored levels (Lagoon, Foundry, Catacombs; 3840×2560 units, twelve rooms each), a start screen, a walkable waiting room with host map choice and readiness, chest puzzles, survival gear, flooding, hunters and a web export. Rooms of two, three and four players are exercised by local socket tests, and the browser sessions the repo records used two clients on one computer.

Every check the repo records is local: headless Godot suites, a real-socket runner with a delayed relay, native renders and browser captures. The records list no WAN playtest, no public deployment and no human balance session. The history is nine commits over seven calendar days, 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-12.
narrative.lessons:
What the repo's records say is still open or was learned.

Open: human multi-person balance (round pacing, flood frequency, hunter pressure, gear value, room density, extraction fairness), real WAN latency, public TLS deployment, other browsers, and reconnect or host migration. Hunter spawn and pathfinding quality are not established.

Learned, as recorded: the DepthFlow clips barely moved or were rejected when applied to the playable map, and the Atlantis depth background was superseded by the playable-map expansion. A parallel run of legacy render tests lost window focus and produced five downstream failures; a serial run and a focus probe found the cause. A network fixture still asserted a superseded camera zoom and was corrected. The verification record also says its counts describe assertions, not coverage or playtest quality.

evidence.quote: Rules run at 20Hz with recipient-filtered snapshots at 10Hz. Clients and authority share per-match geometry. Movement packets contain direction, sequence and match token, never client positions. Bounded prediction and fractional presentation smooth acknowledgements. Focus loss sends neutral input; stale input stops after 250ms.

Hidden explorer packets omit position, velocity, region and held items; clients clear stale presentation caches. Rival gear, breath, health, exact treasure, puzzle data and hunter routes remain private.
Lagoon, Foundry and Catacombs each contain a 3840×2560 playable ruin, twelve rooms and segmented gated corridors.
Seeded rounds last 10–30 minutes, including a final 60–120-second escape warning.

The network runner rejects script errors and covers fifteen scenarios, including all three large levels with 2/3/4 actual client processes, puzzles, shared provisions, extraction, disconnects and a relay with 200ms round-trip delay plus periodic 180ms stalls. This proves local reliable-transport behavior, not WAN conditions.

The central room service owns movement validation, world objects, flood state, relic ownership, extraction and outcomes. Clients send intentions, not trusted positions, water levels, inventories or scores.

Fresh verification: nine headless suites total 13,364 checks / 0 failures; full network runner 15/15 scenarios, including 2–4 people, latency/stalls and complete rounds on all three levels; production environment GPU 1,236/0; focused door/object GPU 171/0; legacy GPU 23/0 serial; web rebuild and smoke 8/0.

claims.text: Server-side rules advance in fixed 0.05 s steps (20 Hz): TideGame defines STEP := 0.05, and the server-mode session accumulates frame time and calls directory.step() once per step.
Recipient views are sent on every second tick (10 Hz) and immediately after any accepted event; each view is projected for one recipient. The README states 10 Hz recipient-filtered snapshots.

A movement command must have exactly three keys (direction vector, integer sequence, match token). Extra keys such as position or player, non-finite or over-unit components, stale sequences and old match tokens are rejected; the authority test exercises each case.
Seat identity comes from the connection id (room.peers.find(peer)), never from the packet. Requests are budgeted per peer per second (40 movement, 30 other).
The room service caps rooms at 64 and connections at 256; the server README says these are implementation bounds, not proven production capacity figures.

ExpeditionView.project sends an unseen explorer as only a name and the state hidden. A visible rival gets position, velocity, region, state and light/relic flags; breath, score and survival inventory are added only for the recipient's own explorer.

The privacy test passes each recipient's packet through var_to_bytes and bytes_to_var before asserting, then checks that rival health, gear, ammo and treasure, hidden monsters, other players' puzzle nonce and the full simulation state are absent.

Client prediction is bounded: at most 12 unacknowledged commands (MAX_PENDING). Each snapshot drops acknowledged commands, resets to the authoritative position and replays the rest; during a stall the client stops predicting.

Rounds are seeded: the room service draws four bytes of cryptographic randomness at start, and ExpeditionSystems seeds one RandomNumberGenerator that fixes duration (600–1800 s), escape grace (60–120 s), breach, hunt and atmosphere timers and chest rewards.

The rules class (TideGame) is a RefCounted with no scene, timer or input dependency; its header says transport owns time and event order. The repo's guidelines say rules, shared geometry and presentation are kept in separate modules.
Within each step doors advance before water is computed, and a refuge door's permeability is exactly 0.0 when closed, so a refuge that finishes closing while dry admits no water on that tick.
Water moves by simultaneous transfers computed from one previous-state snapshot; each region's total outgoing volume is scaled so it cannot exceed what the region holds.

Hunters are spawned one per active explorer and each keeps one target. A hunter leaves when its target is inactive, more than 900 units away, or unseen for a 50-tick (2.5 s) search; the next hunt is rolled 125–200 s after the last hunter leaves.

The room service is a headless Godot process (server/room_server.gd) running the same session script in server mode. A Node script (web/serve.mjs) serves the web export, forwards WebSocket upgrades on /rooms to loopback and spawns the Godot server as a child process.
The README describes three levels (Lagoon, Foundry, Catacombs), each a 3840×2560 playable ruin with twelve rooms and segmented gated corridors, and seeded rounds of 10–30 minutes.

The product document assigns movement validation, world objects, flood state, relic ownership, extraction and outcomes to the central room service; clients send intentions, not positions, water levels, inventories or scores.

The repo reports, in a section dated 8 October 2026, nine headless suites totalling 13,364 checks with 0 failures and 15 of 15 real-socket network scenarios; another section the same day lists per-suite counts (rules 643, privacy 77, authority 53). Not re-run here.

The network runner covers fifteen scenarios, including a relay with 200 ms round-trip delay and periodic 180 ms stalls; the README states this proves local reliable-transport behaviour, not WAN conditions.

Paid PixelLab submissions are guarded by receipts: a receipt in state 'submitting' is written before the POST, an existing receipt blocks a second POST, and only a rate-limited receipt with an identical payload may be resubmitted.
The repo records PixelLab usage as allowance changes: 82 generations for the first model, 124 for the grip and pickup extension, and 85 units for the brine stalker, with no dollar price inferred.
The hunter ('brine stalker') sprite set is a PixelLab original with 256 frames and 32 tags across eight directions (walk 12, idle 8, attack 8, stun 4).
The explorer sprites ship as palette bundles (explorer-holding-pN-v2) of 1,376 frames each on an 88×88 canvas; the docs say PixelLab frames were corrected by local authoring for grips and pickups.
The Atlantis depth map is local Depth-Anything-V2 output (vits, CPU), 1536×1024, near=white; its manifest records the SHA-256 of the source image assets/city.png.

The Atlantis backdrop sat on a separate CanvasLayer behind the playable level and moved up to 10 source pixels on a 24 s loop through a depth-parallax shader with a reduced-motion switch. The repo later marks it superseded.
Sixteen furniture motifs and eight floor-detail motifs were produced with the built-in image_gen tool and are used in all 36 production rooms.
The repository has 9 commits, from 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-12, and the author-email count shows all 9 use one address, the owner's.
No public deployment exists and WAN behaviour is unverified: the server README says no public server or domain exists, and the verification record lists real internet sessions as unverified.

excerpts.title: One fixed step: doors before water
excerpts.code:
func step() -> void:
	if finished: return
	if expedition != null: expedition.before_water(self)
	# Door closure advances before same-tick transfer. A dry, fully sealed R4
	# therefore has exactly zero incoming flow on the threshold tick.
	_advance_vault_holds()
	_advance_doors()
	_advance_valve_holds()
	_advance_water()
	var closed := _closed_doors()
	for who in range(explorers.size()):
		var input: Dictionary = inputs[who]
		var explorer: Dictionary = explorers[who]
		if not _active(who): continue
		var direction: Vector2 = input.direction if tick - input.received_tick < INPUT_TIMEOUT_TICKS else Vector2.ZERO
		if expedition != null:
			if not direction.is_zero_approx(): explorer.facing = direction
			direction *= expedition.movement_factor(self, who)
		var before: Vector2 = explorer.position
		var start_depth: float = water_depths[explorer.region]
		explorer.position = Map.move(before, direction, STEP, closed, start_depth, water_depths, explorer.has_relic, expedition != null and expedition.has_oxygen(self, who))
		explorer.velocity = (explorer.position - before) / STEP
		explorer.region = Map.region_at(explorer.position)
		input.applied_sequence = input.sequence
	_advance_survival_and_extraction()
	if expedition != null: expedition.advance_hunters(self)
	tick += 1
	if not explorers.any(func(explorer): return explorer.state == "exploring"): _finish("all_terminal")
	elif float(tick) * STEP >= (EXPEDITION_LENGTH if expedition == null else expedition.duration): _finish("deadline")
excerpts.why: The comment and the call order carry the rule: doors advance, then water transfers, then movement, survival and hunters. A dry refuge whose door finishes closing in this tick sees a closed door in the same tick's water step.

excerpts.title: Strict input gate and the 20 Hz / 10 Hz loop
excerpts.why: accept_input requires exactly three keys of the right types, so a position or player id in the packet fails the size check. The seat is found from the connection. step() runs the rules once per tick but sends views only when tick % 2 == 0.

excerpts.title: Recipient-specific projection
excerpts.why: Only the observer's own explorer gets breath, score and survival fields. Another explorer appears in full only if the map's sight test passes; otherwise the packet holds a name and the state hidden.

excerpts.title: Bounded prediction and reconciliation
excerpts.code:
func advance(direction: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
	sequence += 1
	var command := {"direction": direction.limit_length(1), "sequence": sequence, "match_id": match_id}
	# Stop prediction during a stalled connection; authority still expires input.
	if pending.size() < MAX_PENDING:
		pending.append(command)
		_move(command.direction)
	return command
func reconcile(snapshot: Dictionary) -> bool:
	if snapshot.match_id != match_id:
		reset(snapshot)
		return true
	if snapshot.tick < tick: return false
	tick = snapshot.tick
	_set_world(snapshot)
	var before := position
	pending = pending.filter(func(command): return command.sequence > snapshot.ack_sequence)
	position = snapshot.explorers[snapshot.you].position
	for command in pending: _move(command.direction)
	correction_distance = before.distance_to(position)
	return true
excerpts.why: advance() sends direction, sequence and match id and predicts only while fewer than MAX_PENDING commands are unacknowledged. reconcile() discards acknowledged commands, takes the server position and replays the pending ones.

excerpts.title: Seeded round parameters
excerpts.code:
func _init(seed_value: int, map) -> void:
	rng.seed = seed_value
	# Weather is rolled once per expedition; its severity sets both cadence and
	# a 10–30 minute duration. All clients observe authority's same clock.
	var weather := rng.randf()
	duration = float(roundi(600.0 + weather * 1200.0))
	escape_grace = float(rng.randi_range(60, 120))
	next_breach = 55.0 + weather * 25.0
	next_hunt = 115.0 + weather * 65.0
	next_atmosphere = 85.0 + weather * 30.0
	var index := 0
	for chest_id in map.chest_anchors:
		var anchor: Dictionary = map.chest_anchors[chest_id]
		# Early provision chests deliberately share map/chart knowledge and supply
		# breathing gear before routes can be cut. Later rewards are seeded.
		var loot: String = ITEM_NAMES[index % ITEM_NAMES.size()]
		chests[chest_id] = {"id": chest_id, "position": anchor.position, "region": anchor.region, "opened": false, "claimed": [], "kind": ["runes", "circuit", "pressure"][index % 3], "loot": loot, "treasure": rng.randi_range(20, 45)}
		index += 1
excerpts.why: One seed fixes the round's weather roll, which sets duration and timer offsets, and the chest rewards. No wall clock or client value enters; the room service supplies the seed.

excerpts.title: Privacy test on serialized packets
excerpts.code:
func packet(game, who: int) -> Dictionary:
	# Assert actual transport-serializable data, rather than trusting node hiding.
	return bytes_to_var(var_to_bytes(View.project(game, who, "private-test")))
func place(game, who: int, position: Vector2) -> void:
	game.explorers[who].position = position
	game.explorers[who].region = game.Map.region_at(position)
func _init() -> void:
	for map_id in Maps.PRODUCTION_IDS:
		var game := Rules.new(7, 3, map_id)
		var own: Dictionary = game.explorers[0]
		var other: Dictionary = game.explorers[1]
		place(game, 0, game.Map.region_center("R0"))
		place(game, 1, own.position + Vector2(0, 110))
		# R3 is distant from R0 on all three layouts; R11 neighbours R0 on
		# the foundry and catacomb routes and is legitimately observable.
		place(game, 2, game.Map.region_center("R3"))
		own.gear.map = true
		own.gear.chart = true
		other.health = 1
		other.gear.gun = true
		other.ammo = 12
		other.treasure = 999
		game.expedition.monsters.assign([{"id": 1, "position": own.position + Vector2(80, 0), "velocity": Vector2.LEFT, "stun_until": -1, "attack_until": -1, "route": [game.Map.region_center("R3")], "target": 2}, {"id": 2, "position": game.Map.region_center("R3"), "velocity": Vector2.ZERO, "stun_until": -1, "attack_until": -1, "route": [own.position], "target": 0}])
		game.expedition.puzzles[1] = {"chest": "T0", "nonce": 778899, "kind": "runes", "sequence": [0, 1, 2, 3], "progress": 1}
		var data := packet(game, 0)
		check(data.map_id == map_id and data.duration >= 600 and data.duration <= 1800, "Public map and clock metadata is accurate")
		check(data.explorers[0].health == 3 and data.explorers[0].gear.map, "Own survival inventory is available")
		check(data.explorers[1].has("position"), "Nearby lit rival is observable")
		for field in ["health", "gear", "ammo", "treasure", "tank", "breath", "score", "stun_until", "hurt_until"]:
			check(not data.explorers[1].has(field), "Rival private field excluded: " + field)
		check(data.explorers[2].size() == 2 and data.explorers[2].state == "hidden", "Unseen player has only identity/hidden state")
		check(data.monsters.size() == 1 and data.monsters[0].id == 1, "Hidden monster position never enters packet")
		for field in ["route", "target", "path_tick", "stun_until", "attack_until"]: check(not data.monsters[0].has(field), "Visible monster internals remain private")
		check(data.puzzle.is_empty(), "Another player's puzzle/nonce is not broadcast")
		check(not data.has("inputs") and not data.has("region_areas") and not data.has("event_sequences"), "Snapshot never includes full simulation")
		check(not data.chests.has("T7"), "Hidden treasure chest is not disclosed")
		check(not data.chests.T0.has("loot") and not data.chests.T0.has("treasure"), "Unsolved chest does not disclose inventory reward")
excerpts.why: packet() round-trips the projection through var_to_bytes, so the test inspects what could cross the wire, not node state. The checks list rival fields that must be absent and a hidden monster that must not appear.

excerpts.title: Receipt before a paid request
excerpts.why: The 'submitting' receipt is written before request(). An existing receipt blocks a second POST unless the stored state is rate_limited with an identical payload, so an ambiguous failure cannot cause a duplicate charge.

excerpts.title: Depth-parallax fragment shader
excerpts.why: The grayscale depth map shifts each sample's UV by offset_pixels times (depth minus focus_depth). The shader clamps to half a texel so edges do not wrap. This is the effect the Atlantis colour and depth pair was built for.

demo.note: Runs locally: a Node script serves the Godot web export and proxies /rooms to a headless Godot room service. No public deployment; the server README says none exists.

limitations: No WAN playtest: 'Public HTTPS/WSS, other browser engines, real internet sessions and human balance remain unverified.' (EXPANSION_VERIFICATION.md)
No public deployment: the server README says no public server or domain exists. The game runs locally with a Godot room service on loopback.
Reconnect and host migration are not implemented; leaving, reloading or disconnecting during an active round aborts it.
The delayed-relay tests model reliable TCP delay and stalls, not packet loss; the record says no frame-rate or zero-stutter claim is made.
Human balance and sustained multi-person sessions still need playtesting; numeric tuning is provisional.
Test counts are assertion counts, 'not coverage percentages or human playtest quality'. This site's review re-ran none of the Godot suites, so every count is reported by the repo.
Hunter spawn and pathfinding quality are not established by the repo's evidence.
The Atlantis city backdrop, its depth map and the DepthFlow clips are superseded and are not part of the production levels.
Room, connection and rate limits are implementation bounds, not capacity figures.
Gallery screenshots are untracked working files from the git-ignored test-output/ folder and carry no commit sha.
